Guiding Principles
 • There is no single ‘gold standard’ for producing measures
 of academic growth
 • Decisions are influenced by factors such as:
 – How will results be used?
 – What questions do we want to answer?
 – How will the model support the values and policy priorities?
 – What are the conditions and constraints that influence
 implementation?

 Growth for Accountability

Model decisions should be informed by criteria

• Policy considerations
 – Does the selected approach align with the state’s theory of action for the
 accountability system?
 – Does the model provide information to inform the highest priority questions?
 – Are the expectations for ‘good enough’ growth appropriate and reasonable?
• Technical considerations
 – Are results valid, reliable, and fair?
 – Are relationships with factors thought to be unrelated to growth minimized (e.g. prior
 performance, school size)?
 – Are there sufficient and appropriate assessment data to support the model?
• Practical considerations
 – Are the model features open to inspection and customization?
 – Can it be implemented with current resources?
 – Are results clear and usable to stakeholders?
 – Is the model robust to changes in the assessment(s)?

 Growth for Accountability

Next steps
 • We suggest investing time to articulate the state’s
 priorities for growth to develop criteria related to policy,
 technical, and practical considerations
 • By so doing, the state can develop a set of criteria to
 – Guide model selection
 – Determine model features
 – Inform ongoing evaluation

 Growth for Accountability

Some examples of potential criteria:

 • The state values approaches that:
 – Provide both norm- and criterion-referenced information
 – Detect important school level effects
 – demonstrate availability of the full distribution of growth outcomes to
 schools of various demographic compositions (e.g., poverty, SWD, and
 ELL)
 – appropriate correlations with prior year status
 – Provide clear and usable results
 – Are robust to changes in state assessment and differences in test
 characteristics
 – Are open and transparent
 …etc
